method: Curated unresolved acceptance questions grounded in published source-limited findings and the canonical work queue; no raw capture material.

open_checks: Identify the page bootstrap entrypoints that actually import the conversation feature; classify asynchronous chunk boundaries.
Assign exported handlers to verified module owners rather than lexical proximity.
Resolve or classify remaining cross-bundle aliases and dynamic imports in the selected client paths.
Check field-level invariants across graph mutation, optimistic selection and serialization boundaries.
Trace remaining visible and conditional transcript controls to actual registered handlers.
Finish tracing state consumers and producers beyond the selected message path.
Correlate request construction and decoded response fields across remaining client call sites.
Connect completion, interruption and error callbacks to scoped state and conditional UI output.
Trace error-to-UI propagation and cleanup for each retry, cancellation and terminal branch.
Determine whether full message maps enter browser-persistent stores, separating unrelated cross-tab listeners.
Resolve conditional typed tool/media renderers, hidden-content filters and remaining import boundaries.
Reconcile conditional feature gates and remaining untraced lifecycle edges against the ten-stage source model.
Link component class/state applications to captured stylesheet rules and responsive branches.
Account for remaining chat control handlers and their feature eligibility conditions.
Reconcile alternate graph representations and serialization paths with mutation rules.
Complete chat request/response decoding, stream terminal events and persistence boundaries.
Resolve client gates and untraced source edges from input to rendered output; leave server behavior unknown.

limitations: Open checks are required investigations, not verified failures.
A finding reference demonstrates partial work, not acceptance.
Static-source acceptance does not require or imply runtime execution or backend verification.
